source.original_text: Let M be a Riemannian submanifold of a Euclidean space E with the metric induced by E, and let F:M→ℝ be smooth. Its Riemannian gradient is characterized by DF(x)[v]=⟨v,grad F(x)⟩x for every tangent vector v. For any smooth ambient neighborhood extension f of F, grad F(x)=Proj_x(grad f(x)). For the unit sphere the tangent space at x is the orthogonal complement of the line spanned by x.

lean.statement: ∀ (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)] (x : Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1) (f : E → ℝ) (g : E), HasGradientAt f g (x : E) → ∀ z : (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ, ((∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x, mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1 => f (y : E)) x w = inner ℝ (mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : Metric.sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x w) (z : E)) ↔ z = (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto g)
decoder_context: Metric.sphere (0:E) 1 is the set of vectors with norm1. (ℝ ∙ x)ᗮ is the orthogonal complement of the real linear span of x, with its inherited inner product.
Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E=n+1) supplies the finite-dimensional sphere model dimension. 𝓡 n is the real n-dimensional manifold model.

TangentSpace I x is the abstract tangent type of the manifold modeled on I. mvfderiv I h x is the actual differential of h into a vector space, as a continuous linear map on that tangent type; it is totalized to zero without differentiability.
HasGradientAt f g x certifies a genuine ambient Fréchet derivative represented by the linear functional v↦inner ℝ g v.

The inclusion ((↑):sphere (0:E)1→E) is the literal subtype inclusion. orthogonalProjectionOnto maps an ambient vector into the indicated orthogonal subspace. Subtype coercions send candidate vectors into E.

import Mathlib.Geometry.Manifold.Instances.Sphere
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic

/-!
# The induced gradient on a sphere

The actual derivative of the sphere inclusion identifies chart tangent directions
with the ambient orthogonal tangent plane. Pairing through this inclusion gives
the induced metric, rather than the default inner product on chart coordinates.
A genuine ambient gradient therefore determines the unique tangent representative
of the actual restricted manifold differential by orthogonal projection.
-/

noncomputable section

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereGradient

open Metric
open scoped Manifold InnerProductSpace

variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]

/-- The orthogonal projection of the genuine ambient gradient is exactly the
unique ambient tangent vector representing the true sphere differential with
its induced pairing. No default chart metric is identified with this pairing. -/
theorem sphere_gradient_characterization
    (n : ℕ) [Fact (Module.finrank ℝ E = n + 1)]
    (x : sphere (0 : E) 1) {f : E → ℝ} {g : E}
    (hf : HasGradientAt f g (x : E)) :
    ∀ z : (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ,
      ((∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
        mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => f (y : E)) x w =
          ⟪mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x w, (z : E)⟫_ℝ) ↔
        z = (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ.orthogonalProjectionOnto g) := by
  let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ
  let A := mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x
  have hA : A.range = K := range_mvfderiv_subtypeVal x
  have hco := (contMDiff_coe_sphere (n := n) (m := 1) x).mdifferentiableAt one_ne_zero
  have hd : ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => f (y : E)) x w =
        ⟪A w, g⟫_ℝ := by
    intro w
    have hchain := mvfderiv_comp x hf.differentiableAt.mdifferentiableAt hco
    change mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (f ∘ ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E)) x w = _
    rw [hchain]
    convert! (hf.fderiv_apply (y := A w)) using 1 <;>
      simp [A, mvfderiv, NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace, real_inner_comm] <;> rfl
  have hp : ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => f (y : E)) x w =
        ⟪A w, (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g : E)⟫_ℝ := by
    intro w
    have hw : A w ∈ K := hA ▸ (show A w ∈ A.range from ⟨w, rfl⟩)
    rw [hd w]
    exact (K.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_left ⟨A w, hw⟩ g).symm
  intro z
  constructor
  · intro hz
    apply ext_inner_left ℝ
    intro v
    have hv : (v : E) ∈ A.range := hA.symm ▸ v.property
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hv
    change ⟪(v : E), (z : E)⟫_ℝ = ⟪(v : E), (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g : E)⟫_ℝ
    rw [← hw]
    exact (hz w).symm.trans (hp w)
  · rintro rfl
    exact hp

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.SphereGradient

lesson.title: The induced gradient on the sphere is a projection
lesson.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space of dimension n+1 and let x be on its unit sphere. If the ambient objective f has genuine gradient g at x, its restriction F to the sphere has a unique ambient tangent representative of its actual manifold differential. That representative is the orthogonal projection of g onto T=x⊥. The pairing uses the actual inclusion derivative Aₓ, so it specifies the induced metric rather than a default chart inner product.
lesson.formula: T=(\mathbb R x)^\perp,\quad A_x=D\iota(x),\quad F=f\circ\iota,\qquad DF(x)[w]=\langle A_xw,z\rangle_E\ \forall w\ \Longleftrightarrow\ z=P_Tg\quad(z\in T).
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space; dim E=n+1 and n may be0. Finite dimension supplies completeness and closedness of the tangent subspace, so no extra analytical premise is added.
x lies on the unit sphere, and f:E→ℝ has a genuine gradient g at x. Source smoothness implies this pointwise HasGradientAt witness; the theorem explicitly allows weaker pointwise regularity.
F is the literal restriction y↦f(y). Source maps on an ambient open neighborhood can be represented by their local germs, but arbitrary smooth extension construction is not proved.

Mathlib chart tangent directions are sent into the ambient tangent plane by the actual derivative Aₓ of the sphere inclusion. Its exact range is proved by Mathlib and used internally, not assumed. The induced pairing is ⟨Aₓw,Aₓw′⟩E; no default chart norm/inner product is identified with it.

steps.title: Identify actual tangent directions
steps.text: The sphere inclusion is differentiable. Its differential Aₓ has range exactly the ambient plane T orthogonal to x. Thus every actual chart tangent direction maps into T, and every vector in T has a preimage. The companion injectivity theorem makes the pullback of the ambient pairing positive definite; the present ambient-representative proof uses the exact range.
steps.lean:
let K := (ℝ ∙ (x : E))ᗮ
  let A := mvfderiv (𝓡 n) ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E) x
  have hA : A.range = K := range_mvfderiv_subtypeVal x
  have hco := (contMDiff_coe_sphere (n := n) (m := 1) x).mdifferentiableAt one_ne_zero
steps.detail: contMDiff_coe_sphere gives actual differentiability; range_mvfderiv_subtypeVal supplies both directions of the tangent identification. injective_mvfderiv_subtypeVal_sphere is background for interpreting the induced metric, not a call in this proof.

steps.title: Differentiate the actual restricted objective
steps.text: Apply the manifold chain rule to F=f∘ι. The ambient gradient is a genuine derivative witness, so evaluating the result at w gives the ambient pairing with its true direction Aₓw. Explicit vector-space tangent identification reconciles target types; it changes neither the differential nor the metric.
steps.lean:
have hd : ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => f (y : E)) x w =
        ⟪A w, g⟫_ℝ := by
    intro w
    have hchain := mvfderiv_comp x hf.differentiableAt.mdifferentiableAt hco
    change mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (f ∘ ((↑) : sphere (0 : E) 1 → E)) x w = _
    rw [hchain]
    convert! (hf.fderiv_apply (y := A w)) using 1 <;>
      simp [A, mvfderiv, NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace, real_inner_comm] <;> rfl
steps.detail: mvfderiv_comp and HasGradientAt.fderiv_apply provide the mathematical equalities. NormedSpace.fromTangentSpace is the explicit trivial-vector-space tangent identification; convert/rfl only reconciles its identity map.

steps.title: Remove the normal component
steps.text: For each w, Aₓw belongs to T. Orthogonal projection changes g only by a vector perpendicular to T, so it preserves this pairing. The projected vector is already typed in T, furnishing an actual candidate gradient representative.
steps.lean:
have hp : ∀ w : TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x,
      mvfderiv (𝓡 n) (fun y : sphere (0 : E) 1 => f (y : E)) x w =
        ⟪A w, (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g : E)⟫_ℝ := by
    intro w
    have hw : A w ∈ K := hA ▸ (show A w ∈ A.range from ⟨w, rfl⟩)
    rw [hd w]
    exact (K.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_left ⟨A w, hw⟩ g).symm
steps.detail: Submodule.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_left applies to the proved tangent membership. No differential equality for the candidate is supplied as a premise.

steps.title: Prove uniqueness on the whole tangent plane
steps.text: Suppose a tangent candidate z has the same differential pairings for every chart direction. Given any v in T, use the exact-range identity to choose w with Aₓw=v. The two candidates pair equally with every v in T. Nondegeneracy of its inherited inner product gives z=P_Tg. Conversely, the projected candidate satisfies all pairings by the preceding step.
steps.lean:
intro z
  constructor
  · intro hz
    apply ext_inner_left ℝ
    intro v
    have hv : (v : E) ∈ A.range := hA.symm ▸ v.property
    obtain ⟨w, hw⟩ := hv
    change ⟪(v : E), (z : E)⟫_ℝ = ⟪(v : E), (K.orthogonalProjectionOnto g : E)⟫_ℝ
    rw [← hw]
    exact (hz w).symm.trans (hp w)
  · rintro rfl
    exact hp
steps.detail: Range surjectivity supplies each test direction; ext_inner_left proves uniqueness in the ambient tangent subspace. This constructs the candidate and proves its characterization before defining any chosen gradient object.

lesson.lean_statement: TangentSpace (𝓡 n) x is the actual Mathlib tangent type for the unit sphere. mvfderiv is the true vector/scalar-valued manifold differential. z is in the ambient orthogonal tangent subspace; all w are quantified. The conclusion is a characterization, so it supplies existence by setting z=P_Tg and uniqueness for any candidate.
lesson.lean_proof: Use the actual sphere inclusion and manifold chain rule, remove the normal component with projection, then test every ambient tangent direction through the exact range. No project-owned gradient definition or fallback semantics are introduced.

reconstruction.text:
Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive group structure. For every natural number n with dim_R(E) = n + 1, every x on the unit sphere S = {u in E : ||u|| = 1}, every function f : E -> R, and every vector g in E, suppose f has a genuine ambient Frechet derivative at x represented by v |-> <g,v>. Put L = (R x)^perp. Then for every candidate z in L the following are equivalent:
(1) For every abstract tangent vector w in T_x S, using the real n-dimensional manifold model, the differential of the restricted function f|_S at x evaluated on w equals <d(iota)_x(w), z>, where iota : S -> E is the literal inclusion and z is coerced into E for the pairing.
(2) z is exactly the orthogonal projection of g onto L, with both sides regarded as elements of L.
Thus the projection is the unique vector in the orthogonal complement of x that represents the restricted differential through the inner product induced by the inclusion. The pairing uses the ambient image d(iota)_x(w); it does not identify the candidate's subtype with the abstract tangent type by an unstated equality. The differential expressions are the specified mvfderiv operators, which return zero when differentiability is absent. In this sphere setting the ambient HasGradientAt hypothesis gives differentiability of the restriction at x, and the inclusion is differentiable, so the characterization concerns genuine differentials at that point, rather than freely supplied linear maps or a condition that holds merely because a nondifferentiable map has a totalized zero derivative.
The claim is local at x. It assumes no global smoothness of f, imposes no positivity or nonzero condition on g or z, and includes n = 0 (ambient dimension one). It asserts an exact iff for all candidates z, not just that the projected candidate satisfies the pairing identity. It gives no differential equation, convergence bound, global gradient field, or formula for derivatives away from x.
